job.title: Senior Accounts Receivable Officer
job.description:
Senior Accounts Receivable Officer
Permanent, Full Time | Lower North Shore, Sydney
Hybrid Work Arrangement

Job Brief
Our client is looking for a Senior Accounts Receivable Officer to look after billing and collections across a portfolio of resident accounts. Billing is largely automated, so the focus of this role is working with the accounts that need attention and having conversations that call for empathy and a steady hand. It suits someone with consumer collections experience who wants a clear pathway into an AR Manager role.
 
About Our Client
Our client is a well established not for profit organisation. The finance team is close knit, social and supportive, and people help each other out when things get busy. The business is currently bringing its finance operations together under a new structure, which is creating room for people to grow.
 
Responsibilities
  • Manage collections across resident accounts, working through overdue balances by phone, in person and through payment plans
  • Handle sensitive conversations with residents and their families about fees, helping them understand their bill and how aged care fees work
  • Process monthly charges, receipts, credits, refunds and direct debit runs in the finance system
  • Keep resident billing records accurate, update fees and subsidies, and support the reconciliation of government funding against payment statements
  • Reconcile cash receipts to bank statements and support month end with reconciliations and reporting on overdue and large debts
  • Maintain bond and loan registers and keep resident contract records up to date
  • Meet with families at village sites when needed, with pool cars available
  • Work closely with the wider finance team, customer relations and village administration staff
Requirements
  • 3+ years of experience in accounts receivable or collections, ideally at a senior level
  • Consumer (B2C) collections experience, where you have dealt directly with individuals and families rather than businesses
  • Experience from education, aged care, NDIS, home care or similar consumer billing environments desirable.
  • Resilience and empathy in equal measure, with the confidence to hold firm on difficult conversations while finding workable solutions
  • Strong reconciliation skills and attention to detail
  • Good Excel skills and experience working in a finance system, with Epicor an advantage
  • A driver's licence is an advantage for site visits
What's on Offer
  • Hybrid working with 2 to 3 days from home once settled in, and extra family leave days on top of annual leave
  • A clear pathway to AR Manager as the AR function grows
  • A supportive, social finance team with a strong culture and a structured induction
Apply via link or contact Carolina for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Global RGM Manager
job.description:
This is a cracker of a 6-month, fixed-term Global RGM Manager contract with an FMCG business, based in Sydney's CBD (three days a week in-office) on a salary of circa $170k plus super. It's an immediate start, running through to approximately end of April 2027. You'll report directly to the Global RGM Director, joining at a genuinely early point as Revenue Growth Management is stood up as a proper standalone global function — moving well beyond the pricing-only remit it's historically had in some markets.

The role is a genuine blend: you'll act as commercial business partner to regional teams across the globe on a prioritised project basis, while also playing a central role in building the frameworks, playbooks, and technology foundations the wider function will run on. There's real autonomy here to shape how things get done, not just execute someone else's playbook.

What the role looks like
  • Lead the deployment of global RGM frameworks, tools, and processes across international markets, with an initial focus on strategic pricing.
  • Partner directly with regional commercial teams to identify and prioritise value-creation opportunities across pricing, promotions, trade investment, product mix, and pack-price architecture.
  • Own the development of robust business cases and implementation plans for key RGM initiatives, tracking delivery against agreed milestones and value targets.
  • Turn market, customer, consumer, and competitor data into commercially actionable insight and recommendations for senior stakeholders.
  • Build and roll out RGM capability across the business — training, coaching, and playbooks that lift the maturity of the function globally.
  • Partner across Finance, Marketing, Sales, and Category to embed RGM thinking into planning and pricing decisions, and help standardise how it's measured and reported.
What you'll need
  • 5+ years' experience in Revenue Growth Management, commercial finance, category, pricing, or a related commercial strategy role.
  • Strong grounding in core RGM levers — pricing, promotions, trade investment, product mix, and pack-price architecture.
  • Genuine curiosity and a willingness to challenge — someone who digs into why the numbers say what they do, not just what they say.
  • Proven ability to influence senior, cross-functional stakeholders without direct authority, and to hold a strong view while staying genuinely open to theirs.
  • Advanced Excel and PowerPoint skills; exposure to Power BI or similar analytics tools is a plus.
  • Comfortable rolling up your sleeves with the detail — this isn't a role where you sit above the modelling.
What makes this worth your time
  • Genuine autonomy to help shape how a newly formalised global function operates, from the ground up.
  • Direct exposure to senior leadership — this role reports straight into the Global RGM Director.
  • A genuinely engaged set of stakeholders who'll challenge you and expect to be challenged back.
  • Immediate start available.
This process will move fast — so if you're the right fit, don't wait. Apply now or reach out to Dave Goldbach for a confidential conversation.

job.title: Financial Controller
job.description:
Across dozens of countries, this business ended up with a different reconciliation standard in every location — inconsistent, patchy, risky. This role exists to make Record-to-Report one global process, not fifty local ones.

This is a newly created Global R2R Controller role — genuinely flexible on WFH, with a circa $250K package (inclusive of super) plus an STI. You'll join a large, global professional services organisation with a significant offshore shared services footprint, reporting to the Group Financial Controller. Record-to-Report here has never had a single global owner, and this is that role: first-generation standards and a first-generation control framework, built from scratch across a genuinely international, multi-currency footprint.

What the role looks like
  • Design and own the global R2R standards — month-end close model and calendar, journal policies, balance sheet reconciliation standards, and intercompany accounting — across a multi-country, multi-currency footprint.
  • Build and own the R2R control framework, including key controls, evidence and audit trail requirements, testing cadence, and segregation of duties, as the single source of truth for how R2R is done globally.
  • Provide second-line governance and oversight of R2R execution across an offshore shared services centre and regional finance teams — monitor compliance, approve exceptions, and act as final decision-maker on standards.
  • Own the monthly close model end to end — calendar, sign-offs, workflows — and drive continuous improvement in close speed and predictability without adding risk.
  • Lead the global R2R improvement agenda, including where automation genuinely reduces manual effort, and act as gatekeeper for process and system changes touching close or reconciliations.
  • Be the primary point of contact for internal audit on R2R findings, driving root-cause fixes rather than one-off remediation.
What you'll need
  • A senior finance leader with genuine end-to-end Record-to-Report experience — not just the reporting half or the reconciliation half, but both, and how they connect.
  • Strong technical controllership and big 4 audit background with ASX experience, and with a real understanding of risk, control effectiveness, and balance sheet integrity.
  • Experience operating in a global shared services model — you know how to influence outcomes through people who don't report to you.
  • Background in a large, complex, international business with multi-currency exposure; experience in engineering services, or project-based services environments is well regarded.
  • Comfortable owning an unstructured, self-directed mandate — you'll be defining the job as you go, not following a fixed monthly checklist.
  • Hands-on enough to open a reconciliation and know immediately whether it's right, even though you won't be the one doing them day to day.
What makes this worth your time
  • A genuine blank-canvas mandate — refresh and own the global R2R standards from the ground up rather than inherit someone else's framework.
  • Broad influence across a genuinely global finance function, with 1 direct report and no large team overhead to manage.
  • Flexible WFH, with no mandated in-office days.
  • Immediate start available.
This process will move fast — so if this is the kind of mandate you've been looking for, apply now or reach out to Dave Goldbach for a confidential conversation.

job.title: Senior Treasury Manager - Project & Asset Finance
job.description:
Overview

 We're working with a business at the centre of the digital and energy infrastructure build-out, operating in a sector absorbing very large amounts of capital right now. The financing is constant, and the assets are significant. What the business needs is someone to run the treasury function that sits behind those facilities properly, and to build the processes that will hold as it scales.

It's a hands-on operational treasury role with genuine technical depth, and the person who takes it will end up knowing the underlying business model better than almost anyone.

The role
  • Manage the existing facilities day to day. Key terms, rate sets, interest accruals, fee amortisation, and the monthly compliance cycle including covenant certificates and lender reporting
  • Run the cash waterfall. Facility payments, transfers to and from liquidity accounts, controlled account reconciliations and minimum balance requirements
  • Own weekly funding and cash forecasting across project-level and corporate requirements, with the FX that goes alongside it
  • Manage the hedging operations. Confirmations, settlements, ISDA documentation, valuations and hedge accounting support, working with the GM Treasury on strategy
  • Maintain and update the covenant model, and produce the monthly reporting that lenders, equity investors and SPV arrangements require
  • Bank guarantees, counterparty credit reporting, KYC and treasury controls
  • Lead the treasury management system implementation, automated bank feeds and straight-through processing
What we're looking for
  • Five or more years across corporate treasury, project finance operations or structured finance
  • Project or asset-level financing experience, not just group facilities. This is the requirement that matters most. If you've managed a real facility with real CPs, a real waterfall and real covenant tests, you'll recognise this role immediately
  • Comfort with the financial model. You'll be updating covenant models and reconciling them to reporting, so this needs to be a strength rather than something you delegate
  • Working knowledge of FX and derivatives, ISDAs, confirmations, settlements and hedge accounting support
  • Strong systems capability across ERP, banking platforms and treasury systems, and an interest in automating what's currently manual
  • Control discipline and attention to detail. A lot of what you produce goes to lenders, so accuracy is the baseline
Worth being direct about one thing. This is an operational treasury role rather than a transaction one. If your background is entirely on the bank side and what you want is deal execution, this probably isn't the right fit.

Why apply
  • A business growing quickly in a sector with global relevance and very few precedents
  • Real ownership. You'd be building the treasury function rather than maintaining someone else's
  • Founder-led, accessible leadership, and decisions that get made in days rather than quarters
For a confidential conversation, apply via the link or reach out to Kunal Gupta directly at kunalg@axr.com.au.

job.title: Head of Client Partnerships
job.description:
You've built large revenue portfolios. You've led leaders. You've managed complexity without letting it become chaos.

But you're looking for something bigger than simply hitting a number.

We're partnering with a high-growth Australian business that sits at the intersection of commerce, marketing and customer strategy. In just a few years, it has become a major player in its category and is now focused on its next chapter of growth.

They're looking for a Head of Client Partnerships to lead a significant commercial portfolio, a team of experienced people leaders, and a customer base that includes some of the country's largest organisations.

This is not a role where you'll inherit a perfectly polished machine. The business has scaled quickly. The opportunity now is to bring greater consistency, capability and strategic thinking to a high-performing team while continuing to drive ambitious growth targets.

There are three big pieces to the role:
  • You'll own the operational rhythm of a large and complex commercial portfolio. Hundreds of customer opportunities move through the business at any given time. You'll create visibility, discipline and predictability, ensuring the right priorities get attention and leaders stay focused on what matters most. 
  • Second, you'll develop a group of people leaders who are talented, capable and still growing as managers. You'll coach them on performance management, feedback, accountability and leadership fundamentals. Success will be measured not simply by revenue outcomes, but by the quality of leadership capability you build beneath you.
  • Third, you'll help shift customer conversations to a different level. Today, many relationships are strong commercially. The next horizon is becoming a genuine strategic partner. That means understanding the customer's broader objectives, engaging more effectively with marketing and brand stakeholders, and helping teams move from selling products to solving business problems.
The person who succeeds in this role will be equally comfortable discussing commercial performance, customer strategy, organisational capability and leadership development.

You'll work for a highly respected executive who is known for setting high standards, backing talented people and developing future leaders.
The culture is ambitious, fast-moving and direct.

People who thrive here are naturally curious, commercially sharp and energised by building things. They're accountable, action-oriented and comfortable operating at pace. They don't wait for someone else to solve a problem.

Importantly, this business offers genuine career opportunity. It has ambitious growth plans, significant investment behind it and a track record of promoting strong performers into broader leadership roles.

You'll likely bring:
  • Experience leading leaders, not just individual contributors.
  • Ownership of a significant commercial portfolio, P&L, client book or customer business.
  • The ability to influence senior stakeholders internally and externally.
  • Strong commercial acumen combined with an interest in strategy, marketing or customer growth.
  • A track record of creating clarity, discipline and accountability in fast-moving environments.
  • A reputation for giving honest feedback, building capability and lifting performance.
Background is less important than capability.

You might come from FMCG, media, retail, technology, marketplaces, e-commerce or another customer-led commercial environment.

What matters most is your ability to lead through complexity, create momentum and help a business move from good to great.

job.title: Group FP&A Lead
job.description:
The business

Large-scale infrastructure development. Multiple assets under construction, global institutional backing, and a lot of capital going out the door.
The economics are what make it interesting. Big upfront spend, long-dated contracted revenue, and a lag before asset earnings. There's no long history to extrapolate from and no settled view of unit economics yet. Someone has to build that view and then defend it to investors, lenders and the board.

The role

You'll own the budget and forecast cycle, help build the model that links the construction program to the financial outcome, and produce the reporting the executive actually runs the business off.

The first year is mostly building:
  • The group planning model from scratch. Capex phasing, funding drawdown, the ramp from an asset going live to full contribution
  • A budget and reforecast cycle that gets better each time it runs
  • The metrics that define performance here, and executive agreement on them
  • A planning tool. Right now it's spreadsheets, and that won't hold
  • Board and investor reporting that stands up to institutional scrutiny
Who it suits

There are two routes in, and we're open on both.
You might come from a scale-up, where you built the reporting function yourself and worked without much precedent. The thing to be honest with yourself about is the balance sheet. This business carries a very large asset base and revenue turns up after the spend.

Or from infrastructure, energy, resources or transport, where you've modelled projects from investment decision through construction to revenue. Then the question is pace. There's no process to inherit here and no team of analysts (yet), and decisions happen faster than they do inside a large corporate.

Either works. What matters more is whether you've built something before. If your best work has been running a well-oiled cycle someone else designed, this will frustrate you.

What you'll bring
  • CA, CPA or CFA, or the equivalent in experience
  • Evidence you've built FP&A capability rather than maintained it. What you inherited, what you built, what changed
  • Driver-based modelling across capex, funding and long-dated revenue, not just P&L
  • You've implemented or rebuilt a planning tool
  • The confidence to bring a view to an executive team, not just a number
Apply here with your CV, or email Kunal Gupta at [axr] Recruitment & Search to learn more - kunalg@axr.com.au.

job.title: Regional Sales Manager
job.description:
This is not your standard Regional Sales Manager role.
  
This role is as much about the adventure as it is the career opportunity.
  
It’s the chance to live and work in Papua New Guinea, experience a uniquely fascinating culture and commercial environment and make a genuine impact in one of the country’s most established businesses.
  
Based in Lae, you’ll lead Pacific Industries’ second-largest sales region, build the capability of a sizeable field team and play an important role in the continued growth of the business.
  
Pacific Industries is one of Papua New Guinea’s most established food and beverage businesses and the exclusive PepsiCo bottler in the country. The business grew 70% in FY25 and is up a further 20–25% this year, with a portfolio spanning Pepsi, Mountain Dew, 7UP, Mirinda and Pepsi Max alongside its own iconic local brands.
  
The right person won’t see relocating to Papua New Guinea as simply part of the job. It will be part of the reason they want it.
  
Additional benefits include fully furnished secure accommodation, a company 4WD for business and personal use, an annual return flight to Australia and yacht club membership.
  
What you’ll do

Based in Lae and reporting to the National Sales Manager, you’ll lead the Momase region across Lae, Madang, Wewak and Vanimo, with responsibility for a team of approximately 20–30 sales representatives and merchandisers.
  
This is hands-on commercial leadership, focused on developing the team, improving execution and unlocking the significant growth opportunity that exists across the region.
  
Specific responsibilities include:
  • Leading, coaching and developing the regional sales team
  • Improving trade execution across pricing, planograms, call schedules, share of shelf and in-store standards
  • Building relationships across wholesalers, distributors and independent retailers
  • Using data and commercial insight to identify and unlock growth opportunities
  • Establishing stronger sales reporting, forecasting and performance rhythms
  • Improving debtor management, collections and route-to-market effectiveness
  • Working closely with warehousing and logistics across a complex distribution network
  
You’ll need the following experience and skills
  • Regional or State Sales Management experience within FMCG
  • Experience leading field sales teams across independent, wholesale or distributor channels
  • A track record of coaching people, building capability and managing performance
  • Strong commercial, analytical and customer management skills
  • A solid understanding of trade execution and what great looks like in-store
  • Resilience, adaptability and the ability to operate effectively in a different cultural and commercial environment
  • Most importantly, a genuine commitment to relocating to Lae for at least two years
  
Pacific Industries is looking for someone who can develop capability in others, tell a compelling story through data, persevere when things aren’t straightforward and make the complex simple.
  
About the company

Pacific Industries has been manufacturing and distributing food and beverages in Papua New Guinea since 1936. Today, the third-generation family business employs approximately 800 national staff and 50 expatriates across eleven branches and two manufacturing plants.
  
Since securing the exclusive PepsiCo bottling licence for Papua New Guinea in 2018, the business has entered a significant period of growth and investment, including a new Port Moresby bottling plant commissioned in November 2024.
  
Curious?

If you’re an FMCG sales leader who knows how to build teams, lift execution and grow a region and the idea of doing it in Papua New Guinea excites you, this could be your next great career decision and your next adventure.
  
Start a conversation with Pacific Industries’ chosen recruitment partner for this role, [axr] Recruitment & Search, by hitting the Apply button now.
